_note: Safety is the nurse in the field and the patient in trouble: visit check-in timers, panic with a time-bound live location, patient SOS, next-of-kin nomination and alerting, safeguarding reports, Sentinel deviations at tiers one to three, and the security incident register the identity service already keeps. Wave 2 contract; Waves 3 to 5 build.

refusals.statement: Nothing is dispatched without a human, except for an unresponsive patient or an SOS.
refusals.why: High specificity for dispatching paramedics; a human confirms (§13). Which dispatch happens without a human, and which does not, is packages/catalog/sos-press.json engine.dispatchWithoutAHuman. POST /v1/safety/sos@2 answers it for a fall or a crash a phone noticed with nobody pressing: that is not an SOS, and it does not show a patient is unresponsive.

refusals.statement: A consumer wearable alone never raises dispatch.
refusals.why: BYO signals guide conversation; certified devices carry clinical weight.

refusals.statement: Next of kin see plain language, never clinical detail.
refusals.why: §15. An attempt carries the nomination and the SOS and nothing else; what it would say is packages/catalog/sos-press.json nextOfKin.alertSays, word for word. Anything sent beside them is refused before the attempt is recorded, because the handler sees only the names of undeclared fields and cannot tell a note from a reading.

refusals.statement: A location is not kept after the incident window.
refusals.why: A safety feature that keeps positions is a tracking system. The area an SOS was pressed from is dropped from Safety's store when the window it was pressed under ends, or at the stand-down, and a read after either is refused.

refusals.statement: Safety is timing no visit by that reference.
refusals.why: A timer starts only when Safety hears appointment.in_progress@2. An act on a reference it never started is refused rather than recorded against nothing.

refusals.statement: That visit's timer is held by the nurse who first acted on it. Nobody else extends it, says she is safe or checks her out.
refusals.why: appointment.in_progress@2 names no nurse, so Safety cannot know whose visit a timer is when it starts one. The first identified nurse to act on it holds it and anybody else is refused. A mistake then leaves the timer running, so it pages the desk rather than silencing it.

refusals.statement: That visit is checked out. Nothing is being timed.
refusals.why: A closed timer does not reopen; a new visit starts a new one.

refusals.statement: There is no panic by that reference.
refusals.why: The desk acts on a panic somebody pressed. A pick-up, a resolution or a position read for a panic nobody pressed is refused rather than recorded against nothing.

refusals.statement: There is no SOS by that reference.
refusals.why: The desk acts on an SOS somebody pressed. An area read or a next-of-kin attempt for one nobody pressed is refused rather than recorded against nothing.

refusals.statement: A guardian cannot nominate, withdraw or alert a next of kin for somebody else. Guardian authority is not proven, and MyThuso cannot prove it yet.
refusals.why: docs/governance/INFORMATION-OFFICER.md D-10 is open: who may act for a child or a dependent adult, and what proves it, is undecided, and packages/catalog/vetting.json refuses guardian access until identity and legal authority are both proven. A guardian naming who is told when somebody presses SOS is exactly that authority asserted and recorded as if it were proof. The guardian is admitted to these routes only so that the refusal is this sentence rather than a general one, and it is asked before anything else.

ownIds.why: An incident in the register Safety keeps.

routes.summary: Start a visit timer.

request.why: Chosen by the caller. The same key twice is the same act once.
The visit timed.
How long the visit should take.

response.why: The check-in.
When it goes overdue.

refusals.statement: That visit is not yours to time.
refusals.why: A timer belongs to the nurse at the door.

refusals.statement: A visit is timed by the service that was booked, not by a number sent with it.
refusals.why: The duration lives in packages/catalog/services.json (packages/catalog/field-safety.json, timer.expectedMinutesFrom). A caller-chosen duration is a timer that can be set to anything.

routes.emitsNoneBecause: A timer emits checkin.overdue when it runs out, not when it starts.

withdrawn.why: It started a visit timer from minutes a phone sent. Since Wave 3 Safety starts every timer when it hears appointment.in_progress@2, which Care publishes only once the visit code has matched, timed by the service booked; the nurse reads it on GET /v1/safety/checkins@1 and acts on it through extend@2, safe@1 and close@2, and a locum or a responder on a visit arrives through the same event. Nothing is left for a phone to start. A second way to start a timer would be a timer with a caller-chosen duration, which expected-minutes-not-the-service refuses, or a timer for a visit whose code never matched, which timer-without-a-matched-code refuses. Its correction is the event rather than a route, so that is what it names, and the capability it was cited for is cited on the read that now serves it.

routes.summary: Extend a visit timer.

request.why: Chosen by the caller. The same key twice is the same act once.
The check-in.
How much longer.

response.why: The new deadline.

refusals.statement: That is as long as a visit can run without the desk calling.
refusals.why: An endless extension is a timer that never fires.

routes.emitsNoneBecause: Extending is a check-in, and a check-in is not news.

withdrawn.why: It carried how many minutes and not why. An extension without a reason is a snooze the desk cannot judge, and the refusal extension-without-reason could not be answered through it. Version two carries the reason, one of packages/catalog/field-safety.json extensionReasons, and takes its steps and ceiling from the settings the timer started under.

refusals.why: Closed once.

withdrawn.why: Its only refusal was that a check-in was already closed. It could not refuse a reference Safety never started timing, or a nurse checking out a visit whose timer another nurse holds, and a frozen route cannot gain a refusal without a new version. Version two answers both.

The settings version the timer started under. A change made since reaches the next visit, never this one.
How many more minutes she may ask for before only the desk can let the visit run on.
The steps, in whole minutes, that the settings the timer started under offer and its ceiling still allows.
The last time she said she was safe, when she has. Saying so moved nothing.

refusals.statement: No visit timer is running for that visit. A timer starts when the visit code matches.
refusals.why: Safety times a visit from appointment.in_progress@2 and nothing else. A phone shown a deadline Safety never set is a nurse trusting a clock nobody watches.

routes.emitsNoneBecause: Reading changes nothing.

The check-in.

refusals.why: packages/catalog/field-safety.json checkInRule: an I am safe that carried minutes, or a deadline, would be an extension with no reason and no ceiling, pressed every quarter of an hour.

routes.emitsNoneBecause: Saying she is safe is recorded on her timer and shown to the desk beside an overdue it answers. No engine acts on it, the desk still closes the overdue itself, and the event contract refuses an event nobody reads.

routes.summary: Check out: close the timer.

request.why: Chosen by the caller. The same key twice is the same act once.
The check-in.

response.why: When.

refusals.statement: That check-in is already closed.
refusals.why: Closed once.

routes.summary: The desk picks up an overdue check-in: a person has seen it.

request.why: Chosen by the caller. The same key twice is the same pick-up once.
The overdue check-in.

refusals.why: A pick-up recorded against a timer that never paged the desk is noise in the record a review reads.

routes.emitsNoneBecause: Core lists itself under checkin.overdue@1 and binds no handler for it, so it opens no concern for an overdue check-in that a pick-up could take on, and Care hears the overdue and acts on nothing. The pick-up is the desk's own record that a person saw it, and the event contract refuses an event nobody reads.

routes.summary: The desk closes an overdue check-in it has picked up, with a reason that is true of the timer.

request.why: Chosen by the caller. The same key twice is the same close once.
The overdue check-in.

response.why: When the desk closed it.

refusals.statement: Somebody at the desk picks an overdue check-in up before it is closed.
refusals.why: The record has to say that a person saw it, for a timer exactly as for a panic. It is asked before anything else about the close, so no reason, true or not, closes an overdue nobody picked up.

refusals.statement: An overdue check-in is closed with a reason, or it stays open.
refusals.why: An alarm silenced without a reason is an alarm somebody made stop.

refusals.statement: The nurse has not checked in, extended or checked out, so that cannot be the reason.
refusals.why: The reason is checked against the timer, not taken on trust.

refusals.statement: That check-in is not overdue, so there is nothing here for the desk.
refusals.why: A reason recorded against nothing is noise in the record.

routes.emitsNoneBecause: No engine acts on it. Core lists itself under checkin.overdue@1 and binds no handler for it, so it has no concern for an overdue check-in that a close could stand down, and Care hears the overdue and acts on nothing. The event contract refuses an event nobody reads, so the close is Safety's own record, with its reason.

routes.summary: Press panic: live location to the desk for a fixed window.

request.why: Chosen by the caller. The same key twice is the same act once.
The visit, if there is one.
How long the location is shared.

response.why: The panic.
When sharing stops.

refusals.statement: Live location is shared for a fixed window, and the window always ends.
refusals.why: A share with no end is a tracker.

refusals.statement: The window is the one the desk's policy sets. A phone does not choose how long it is watched.
refusals.why: packages/catalog/field-safety.json declares panic.windowMinutes. A caller-chosen window is a share whose end is whatever was sent.

refusals.statement: A panic goes to the desk. Nobody is sent to it until a person at the desk decides.
refusals.why: §13: never auto-dispatch without a human. The exceptions are an unresponsive patient and an SOS, and a nurse's panic is neither.

routes.summary: The desk picks up a panic: a person has seen it.

request.why: Chosen by the caller. The same key twice is the same pick-up once.
The panic.

response.why: When a person at the desk first picked it up. Picking it up again answers with the same moment.

refusals.statement: That panic is already resolved, so there is nothing to pick up. If she needs help again, a new panic starts.
refusals.why: A resolved panic does not reopen, and a pick-up after it would read as a person answering a panic that was already over.

routes.emitsNoneBecause: A pick-up is Safety's record that a person at the desk saw the panic. Core's concern for the panic is taken on through Core's own acknowledge route by whoever holds it, no engine acts on a pick-up, and the event contract refuses an event nobody reads.

routes.summary: The desk resolves a panic it has picked up, with what happened. Sharing her position stops at once.

request.why: Chosen by the caller. The same key twice is the same resolution once.
The panic.
What happened, as an id from packages/catalog/field-safety.json outcomes. Asked for by the handler rather than the binder, so that a resolution without one is refused in its own sentence.

response.why: When the desk resolved it.
When the desk stopped seeing her position: the resolution, or the window if it had already ended.

refusals.statement: Somebody at the desk picks a panic up before it is resolved.
refusals.why: The record has to say that a person saw it. It is asked before anything else about the resolution, so no outcome resolves a panic nobody picked up.

refusals.statement: A panic is resolved with what happened, or it stays open.
refusals.why: A panic closed with no outcome leaves nothing to review.

refusals.statement: That panic is already resolved. If she needs help again, a new panic starts.
refusals.why: A resolved panic does not reopen, and its window does not come back.

routes.summary: The desk reads where a nurse who pressed panic is, only while her window is open.

request.why: The panic.

routes.emitsNoneBecause: Reading changes nothing.

Where she works, from the roster. Null on this runtime, because Safety holds no roster; never the patient's address.
When the panic was pressed or the deadline passed.
Whole minutes since then.

Whether the position may be read now.
Whether the desk still has something to do.

refusals.statement: No field-safety timing is set to zero or less, whatever its range says.

refusals.statement: Extension steps are listed from the smallest to the largest, each once.

refusals.statement: A patient's Sentinel state is read whole, with no filter.
refusals.why: A filter that hides a suspended baseline or a tier three is a nurse told less than Sentinel knows.

refusals.statement: Sentinel has heard no reading with clinical weight for that patient, so there is no baseline to show.
refusals.why: A patient with no baseline is answered in words rather than with an empty list a nurse could read as all clear.

routes.emitsNoneBecause: Reading changes nothing.

routes.summary: Record a safeguarding concern about a patient — a child, an older person or an adult at risk — by the kind of concern and nothing typed. It is held open for the safeguarding officer, never closes by itself, and is sent to nobody.

request.why: Chosen by the caller. The same key twice is the same concern recorded once.
Who the concern is about, as the opaque token identity issues.
child, older-person or adult-at-risk, from packages/catalog/sentinel.json safeguarding.groups. Asked for by the handler, so a report without one is refused in its own sentence.
The kind of concern, from packages/catalog/sentinel.json safeguarding.categories. A protected category: never a header chip, never on the desk's list and never on the bus. Asked for by the handler.

response.why: The report.
When it was recorded.
open, from packages/catalog/sentinel.json safeguarding.states. A report never closes by itself.
safeguarding-officer-not-on-register, while no safeguarding officer role is on the vetting register.
not-sent, always, while no connection to the South African Police Service or the Department of Social Development exists.
not-integrated, from packages/catalog/sentinel.json safeguarding.statutory.

refusals.statement: A safeguarding report is made by a named reporter.
refusals.why: The safeguarding officer must be able to ask what was seen, so a report from a caller the runtime could not identify is refused before anything is recorded.

refusals.statement: A safeguarding report here holds who it is about, the kind of concern and who recorded it, and nothing typed. What was seen is told to a person, because nothing here has the protections that account needs.
refusals.why: packages/catalog/sentinel.json safeguarding.noNarrative. The runtime hands Safety only the names of undeclared fields, so an account sent under any name is refused before anything is recorded.

refusals.statement: Say whether the concern is about a child, an older person or an adult at risk.
refusals.why: Which Act may require a report depends on who it is about, and a report that cannot say is one nobody can act on.

refusals.statement: Choose the kind of concern from the list.
refusals.why: A kind the contract does not hold is free text by another name.

routes.summary: The desk's list of safeguarding reports: when each was recorded, whether it is about a child, an older person or an adult at risk, that it is open and who it is held for, and that it was not sent. Never the kind of concern, the patient or who made it.

response.why: Every report, newest first.

fields.why: The report.
When it was recorded.
How long it has been open, worked out when the list is read.
Whether it is about a child, an older person or an adult at risk.
open. A report never closes by itself.
Who it is held for, from packages/catalog/sentinel.json safeguarding.officer.
not-sent.
not-integrated.

refusals.statement: A guardian is not told whether a safeguarding report exists or what it says. Guardian authority is not proven, and MyThuso cannot prove it yet.
refusals.why: docs/governance/INFORMATION-OFFICER.md D-10 is open, and a guardian may be the person a report is about. The guardian is admitted to this route only so that the refusal is this sentence rather than a general one, and it is asked before anything else.

refusals.statement: The desk's safeguarding list takes no filter.
refusals.why: A filter by patient or by kind would turn the list into a way to find out who a report is about or what it says.
